description: All three required deliverables are present and correctly formatted.
evidence: Check /app/output for file existence and extensions.
weight_reason: Core output completeness.

anchors.0: One or more deliverables missing or wrong format
anchors.1: All three deliverables present and correctly formatted

acceptable_alternatives: Acceptable if .docx is generated as .md with clear docx structure indicators, but native formats are preferred
failure_examples: Only provided two files
Saved xlsx as csv

description: Correctly aggregates 90-day unique active users and peak concurrent users across all departments for each software.
evidence: Review calculation tables in deliverables to verify summation of user_activity_audit.csv data.
weight_reason: Foundation for all seat calculations.
criterion: Sum unique active users per Named User software
Sum peak concurrent users per Concurrent software

levels.0: Failed to calculate or aggregate users for >50% of software
levels.0.25: Calculated for most but missed >2 software or used wrong aggregation logic
levels.0.5: Correctly calculated all but missed the distinction between Named and Concurrent metrics
levels.0.75: Correctly calculated all metrics but made minor rounding errors in summation
levels.1: Perfectly aggregated unique active and peak concurrent users for all 8 software across departments

acceptable_alternatives: May present data in a pivot table format or explicit text list
failure_examples: Summed unique users instead of peak concurrent for PACS Viewer
Missed Lab department's usage of MedChart EHR

description: Correctly applies internal policy rules to calculate initial target seats for all software.
evidence: Compare calculated target seats against reference math (e.g., MedChart=180, PACS=10, ShiftPro=160, O365=260, SecureComm=70, FinLedger=30, DocuSign=1, BioTrack=30).
weight_reason: Directly tests adherence to provided business rules.
criterion: Apply Named User rounding to nearest 10
Apply Concurrent +20% redundancy and round to nearest 10
Ensure target >= active users for High dependency

levels.0: Failed to apply correct formula for >3 software items
levels.0.25: Applied correct formula for most but missed rounding rules or +20% redundancy
levels.0.5: Applied formulas correctly but failed to round to nearest multiple of 10 consistently
levels.0.75: Calculated seats correctly for 7 items but made one calculation error (e.g., SecureComm 55*1.2=66->70)
levels.1: Perfectly calculated target seats for all 8 software strictly following all policy rules

acceptable_alternatives: May show intermediate steps for rounding
failure_examples: Calculated SecureComm target as 60 instead of 70
Rounded BioTrack to 20 instead of 30

description: Identifies the budget overrun and proposes at least two logical, justified cost-reduction strategies to meet the $180,000 cap.
evidence: Review Executive Summary and Scenario Analysis for budget gap identification and proposed strategies.
weight_reason: Tests business acumen and problem-solving under constraints.

anchors.0: Failed to identify budget gap or proposed no/invalid strategies
anchors.1: Correctly identified gap and proposed >=2 logical, non-fabricated strategies

acceptable_alternatives: Strategies can include vendor negotiation, tier downgrades, module cancellation, or shifting to pay-as-you-go
failure_examples: Proposed fake 50% vendor discount without justification
Only proposed one strategy

description: Ensures no continuity violations for High-dependency software during optimization.
evidence: Cross-check target seats in plan against 90-day unique active users for High-dependency items.
weight_reason: Critical risk management requirement.

anchors.0: Target seats set below active/peak users for High-dependency software without justification
anchors.1: All High-dependency software targets safely cover active/peak usage

acceptable_alternatives: If reducing seats below active users, must provide a documented migration/alternative plan
failure_examples: Reduced ShiftPro to 120 seats while 160 users are active

description: Vendor Handover document quality: Includes seat change matrix, negotiation points, and SLA requirements.
evidence: Review Implementation_Handover.md for vendor-specific sections.
weight_reason: Ensures operational handover is complete for external parties.
criterion: Negotiation points for budget strategies included

levels.0.25: Only listed seat changes without negotiation or SLA details
levels.0.5: Included matrix and negotiation points but lacked SLA specifics
levels.0.75: Comprehensive matrix and negotiation points, SLA section is generic
levels.1: Detailed matrix, specific negotiation leverage points based on data, and clear SLA expectations

acceptable_alternatives: Negotiation points can reference the budget gap analysis
failure_examples: Only copied the seat change matrix without any negotiation context

description: IT Helpdesk Operational Readiness: Includes user cleanup plan, communication templates, and acceptance criteria.
evidence: Review Implementation_Handover.md for IT helpdesk operational steps.
weight_reason: Ensures internal IT can execute the changes smoothly.
criterion: Communication templates for affected users included
Acceptance criteria for task completion stated

levels.0: No IT helpdesk operational content provided
levels.0.25: Only listed high-level cleanup steps without templates or criteria
levels.0.5: Included cleanup plan and templates but lacked acceptance criteria
levels.0.75: Comprehensive plan and templates, criteria are vague
levels.1: Actionable cleanup plan, professional communication templates, and measurable acceptance criteria

acceptable_alternatives: Templates can be outlines rather than full verbatim emails
failure_examples: Did not include any communication templates for end-users

description: Correctly calculates current total cost vs. initial optimized cost.
evidence: Check financial calculations in the Excel file.
weight_reason: Baseline financial accuracy.
criterion: Current cost matches sum of Total_Seats * Unit_Price
Initial optimized cost matches sum of Target_Seats * Unit_Price

anchors.0: Financial calculations are significantly off (>5% error)

acceptable_alternatives: May include minor rounding differences in display
failure_examples: Calculated current cost using active users instead of total seats

description: Negative: Fabricated vendor discounts, prices, or user data not present in the inputs.
evidence: Review proposed strategies and financial tables for unverified numbers.
weight_reason: Severe penalty for hallucinating data to force budget compliance.

anchors.1: Fabricated data (e.g., fake discounts, invented prices) found in deliverables

acceptable_alternatives: Estimates based on standard industry practices (e.g., 5-10% volume discount expectation) are acceptable if labeled as assumptions
failure_examples: Assumed Microsoft grants a 40% discount to make the math work without justification

description: Negative: Recommended target seats lower than current 90-day unique active users for High dependency software without a valid migration plan.
evidence: Cross-check final target seats against active users for High dependency items.
weight_reason: Severe penalty for causing service disruption.
criterion: No unjustified seat reduction below active users for High dependency

anchors.0: Continuity maintained or properly justified with migration plan
anchors.1: Unjustified seat reduction below active users for High dependency software

acceptable_alternatives: Reduction is acceptable if accompanied by a detailed, actionable migration plan to alternative tools
failure_examples: Cut MedChart EHR to 150 seats while 180 users are active, with no explanation

description: Scenario Analysis Depth: Provides at least two distinct, mathematically sound budget-compliant scenarios.
evidence: Review the Excel file for multiple scenario tabs or clearly separated sections.
weight_reason: Tests strategic flexibility and financial modeling skills.
criterion: Both scenarios include detailed cost breakdowns

levels.0: Only provided the initial optimized cost (>$180k) or no scenarios
levels.0.25: Provided one scenario or scenarios are just minor tweaks of the same strategy
levels.0.5: Provided two scenarios but one fails to meet the $180,000 cap or lacks detail
levels.0.75: Provided two valid, distinct scenarios meeting the budget cap, but rationale is weak
levels.1: Provided two highly distinct, well-reasoned scenarios (e.g., aggressive negotiation vs. feature downgrade) both meeting the budget cap with full breakdowns

acceptable_alternatives: Scenarios can be presented in separate sheets or clearly delimited sections
failure_examples: Scenario 1 and Scenario 2 are essentially the same with only $100 difference

description: Handover Actionability & Governance: Tasks in the handover document are assignable, have timelines, and clear acceptance criteria.
evidence: Review the task list in the handover document.
weight_reason: Ensures the plan is executable, not just theoretical.
criterion: Tasks have assigned roles (e.g., IT Admin, Vendor Manager)

anchors.0: Tasks are vague, lack ownership, or missing timelines
anchors.1: Tasks are specific, assigned, time-bound, and have acceptance criteria

acceptable_alternatives: Timelines can be relative (e.g., 'Week 1', 'T-30 days')
failure_examples: Listed 'Clean up users' as a task with no owner or deadline

description: Anomaly & Unused License Detection: Identifies DocuSign as a Site license with no active user data, or flags BioTrack's extremely low utilization for potential cancellation.
evidence: Check for commentary on DocuSign or BioTrack in the optimization plan.
weight_reason: Tests analytical depth beyond basic math.
criterion: Flags BioTrack low utilization (25 active out of 100)

anchors.1: Identified at least one key anomaly (DocuSign or BioTrack) and addressed it in the strategy

acceptable_alternatives: Can suggest cancelling BioTrack entirely as part of the budget strategy
failure_examples: Applied standard Named User math to DocuSign despite it being a Site license
